waiver_targets.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
In his first NFL game, Omar Cooper Jr. played just five offensive snaps and had a 30-yard catch on his only target before sustaining a high-ankle sprain that landed him on IR.

Cooper came off IR in Week 6 and had 6-103-1 on seven targets. His touchdown came on a 48-yard bomb. Cooper also had another touchdown negated by a dubious offensive pass interference penalty called against Jets WR Tim Patrick.

The 30th overall pick in this year's draft, Cooper is a hard-nosed gamer who has good hands and is dangerous after the catch. He can also line up either outside or inside. (Cooper played in the slot on Sunday when the Jets used three-receiver sets.)

Cooper probably isn't going to challenge Garrett Wilson's alpha receiver status on the Jets anytime soon, but he can be an effective No. 2 or No. 3.

Although the Jets will probably be getting Adonai Mitchell back from a finger injury in a week or two, Cooper could be a solution for WR-needy fantasy teams. He has playable matchups against the Dolphins and Raiders the next two weeks.

waiver_targets.name: Michael Mayer
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
The Raiders' passing attack is unconventional in that the team's No. 2 tight end is more fantasy-relevant than the No. 2 wide receiver.

Brock Bowers is not only the Raiders' No. 1 tight end, but the No. 1 tight end in the entire NFL. To Michael Mayer's credit, he's managing to thrive in Bowers' shadow. Mayer actually outproduced Bowers in Week 6, with 7-95-0 on nine targets against the Bills. Bowers had 4-70-0 on nine targets.

Mayer is averaging 5.7 targets, 4.7 catches and 44.7 receiving yards per game. He's playable in a pinch this week and can be a solid backup tight end in leagues where rostering more than one TE makes sense.

waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note: Terrance Ferguson is on IR with an ankle injury but is eligible to come off in Week 8. He could be prominently involved in the Rams' passing game upon his return, particularly if WR Davante Adams misses time with the knee injury he sustained in Week 6.

waiver_targets.name: Jaylen Wright
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note: Ollie Gordon has seized command of Miami's lead-back role, but we shouldn't completely dismiss the possibility that Jaylen Wright plays a fantasy-relevant role at some point. Last season, it was often hard to discern whether Gordon or Wright was the top backup to De'Von Achane. It's clear that Gordon is ahead of Wright on the depth chart now, but it's worth keeping the speedy Wright on the radar and perhaps claiming him if you have a roster spot to spare.

waiver_targets.name: Carolina Panthers
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
Even with injury problems at cornerback, the Panthers' defense proved in Week 6 that it could smother a lesser offense, limiting the Eagles to 14 points and 222 yards of offense.

This week, the Panthers face the Buccaneers, who have been starting undrafted rookie free agent Jalon Daniels at quarterback while Baker Mayfield recovers from a thumb injury. In three starts, Daniels has been sacked nine times and has thrown four interceptions.

Even if Mayfield returns this week, the Panthers will be in play as a streaming defense for Week 6.

waiver_targets.name: Michael Penix Jr.
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
In a week where palatable streaming QB options are limited, Michael Penix Jr. is a solid option.

Penix has thrown for at least 223 yards in all four of his starts this season. After throwing a single TD pass in each of his first three games, he threw for three touchdowns vs. the Bears in Week 6.

Although he's averaging a modest 16.4 fantasy points per start, Penix has been efficient, averaging 8.6 yards per pass attempt. The Falcons are never going to be pass-heavy when they have Bijan Robinson in the backfield, so Penix needs to be efficient to have any fantasy value.

Penix has a tricky matchup this week against a 49ers defense that has given up 6.1 yards per pass attempt and has allowed five TD passes over its first five games. But the 49ers also have the sort of high-powered offense that could force the Falcons into a shootout and pump up the pass volume for Penix.

You could also use Penix against a pass-funnel Buccaneers defense in Week 8 and against the Bengals in Week 9.

waiver_targets.name: Tanner McKee
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
The Eagles' offense is in tatters, with Jalen Hurts on IR with a blood clot in his calf and the Philadelphia offensive line unrecognizable after being so good in recent years and now being so ineffective.

Making his first start of the season in place of Hurts, Tanner McKee was 26-of-45 for 215 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions against the Panthers on Sunday. He averaged just 4.8 yards per pass attempt.

While it's hard to gin up any enthusiasm for McKee or the Eagles' offense, a Week 7 matchup against the Cowboys could make McKee a low-level streaming option. The Dallas pass defense has been atrocious this season, allowing the most fantasy points to opposing QBs.

waiver_targets.name: J.J. McCarthy
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
We have to acknowledge that J.J. McCarthy was a complete train wreck in Minnesota last season and that his splashy performance in relief of Jameis Winston in Week 6 could absolutely be fool's gold.

But sometimes new surroundings can make all the difference, and McCarthy looked like a different player Sunday while almost leading the Giants to a miracle comeback against the Saints.

Last season, McCarthy seemed to want to rocket every throw — even the ones that called for touch. In Week 6, McCarthy looked like more than just a one-speed passer. On the Giants' final drive of the game, McCarthy layered a beautiful throw to TE Isaiah Likely for a 20-yard completion. It was the kind of throw McCarthy seemed incapable of last year.

McCarthy completed 11-of-21 passes for 243 yards with one touchdown and one interception in less than one quarter of action. McCarthy entered the game with 11:31 remaining in the fourth quarter. McCarthy also reminded us that he's a dangerous runner with a 28-yard scramble on his final drive.

Are we on the verge of a McCarthy revival? It's fair to be skeptical. But it might be worth a buck or two to see if McCarthy can finally live up to his first-round draft pedigree.

waiver_targets.name: Dallas Cowboys
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
This might be a hard sell in light of how poorly the Dallas defense has played this season, but the attraction here is a Week 7 matchup with the Eagles.

Plagued by offensive line woes and forced to play without starting QB Jalen Hurts, who has a blood clot in his leg, the Eagles generated only 14 points and 222 yards of offense Sunday against a Carolina defense that isn't regarded as fearsome.

If you're pinching FAAB pennies and want to grab a streaming defense with a zero-dollar bid, consider the Cowboys.

waiver_targets.name: Fernando Mendoza
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note: We don't know what the Raiders' internal timetable is for the switch from veteran QB Kirk Cousins to No. 1 draft pick Fernando Mendoza, but it's possible the team could make that change soon. For the Raiders, this season is all about the transition to Mendoza as the starter. Now that Las Vegas has lost three straight games, any pretense of playoff contention can be set aside. There's no guarantee Mendoza will be a useful fantasy asset in his first handful of NFL starts, but he'll have value in superflex leagues and perhaps in some deeper 1QB formats.
